# Cosimo by Medici & Company

> Grow your business. Not your workload.

Cosimo is an AI agent for financial operations from Medici & Company. It prepares reports, checks, follow-ups, and review packs from existing records. The homepage routes visitors to banks (/banks/), funds (/funds/), and financial service firms (/services/). Bank workflows start with loan activity reviews, borrower review packs, account-file checks, and evidence preparation. Client reporting and document collection are starting points for service firms. Each process requires scoped configuration and testing; bank illustrations do not establish production use at a named bank.

## How the proposed workflow fits a fund team

Start with the records behind one recurring task and an example of the output the team needs. Medici & Company configures and tests the workflow with the team, using its source records, reporting format, and review requirements. Drafts bring the figures and commentary together, with missing information and open questions marked for review. The fund team checks the work, resolves questions, approves the final version, and sends it through its usual process.

The FAQ identifies supported Google Drive, SharePoint, Gmail, Outlook, and Google Calendar connections; task-specific setup and testing are required. SOC 2 certification is on the roadmap, not a current certification. The website does not guarantee implementation time, quantified savings, or audit readiness. Data handling, access, source systems, scope, and commercial terms need to be discussed for the team's proposed setup.

## Insurance workflows to explore

Path: /insurance/

Renewal preparation, submission completeness checks, claims-file summaries, and document follow-ups are starting points to configure and test with insurance teams. These are workflow illustrations, not insurance customer results. Underwriting, pricing, coverage and claims decisions remain with the responsible professionals.

## Fund overview

Path: /funds/

The fund overview introduces three recurring jobs: investor reporting, portfolio updates, and investor requests. An interactive example follows management accounts, company commentary, and a prior report format into a quarterly portfolio update.

The example uses Chianti Capital, the synthetic demo manager. Six companies report $70.0 million in quarterly revenue against a $72.0 million budget. Calderwood's accounts show $9.0 million while its management update says $9.4 million. The draft uses the accounts provisionally and leaves the $400,000 difference visible for review. The example has inspectable source records and a three-page draft. It is authored demonstration content, not a live application run.

## Real estate

Path: /re/

The page focuses on quarterly LP reports, investor statements, capital call notices, and distribution notices. The reporting example uses property figures, manager updates, and investor capital records for fictional Loggia Property Group. Visitors can compare source records with the proposed draft and explore a six-page sample report.

The example preserves open property questions and shows a simplified capital-movement schedule. That schedule excludes income and valuation changes and is not a complete capital account statement. Investor notices use supplied, approved allocations; they do not execute payments.

## Venture capital

Path: /vc/

The page focuses on preparing portfolio and LP updates from founder submissions, company spreadsheets, and fund records. Its fictional Telescope Ventures example contains six companies, five current submissions, one stale submission, and a company with six months of runway at its reported burn rate. An unsigned financing discussion is not treated as cash received.

The six-page example includes portfolio metrics, cash and runway, founder commentary, capital movements, and open items. Company operating figures are not fund performance or valuation measures. The sample capital schedule is incomplete until the necessary approved allocations and adjustments are included.

## Private equity

Path: /pe/

The page focuses on bringing portfolio-company financials, management commentary, and fund records into reporting drafts. Its fictional Chianti Capital example compares company actuals with budgets and explains an EBITDA shortfall from supplied management notes. Unexplained variances and unapproved operating plans remain visible.

The six-page sample includes portfolio metrics, budget comparisons, company updates, capital movements, and review questions. The company totals are management-reported operating figures, not ownership-weighted fund results. The sample does not implement an ILPA reporting template or constitute a complete quarterly financial reporting package.

## Private credit

Path: /credit/

The page focuses on private credit and direct lending: borrower review packs, covenant worksheets, reporting follow-ups, and LP updates. Its fictional Fiorino Debt Partners example follows six loans through servicing data, supplied covenant calculations, and a reporting tracker.

One worksheet shows leverage of 4.80 times using submitted EBITDA and 5.33 times if an unresolved add-back is excluded, compared with a supplied maximum of 5.00 times. This is a review question, not a determination of compliance or default. Another item identifies a missing borrower certificate. Cash interest received and PIK accrued are shown separately; neither is presented as the fund's net return.

The six-page credit pack is an authored example. Agreement definitions, adjustments, testing dates, and exceptions require the credit team's review. Lending decisions remain with the team.

## Hedge funds

Path: /hedge/

The page focuses on investor letters, close-file exceptions, subscription/redemption activity, and allocator response drafts. Its fictional Anamorphic Capital example uses administrator-approved figures and supplied policy records for a long/short equity fund.

The six-page monthly pack separates investor-facing drafts from internal working papers. It includes class returns, an exposure snapshot, investor activity, a cash discrepancy, and a questionnaire response that needs current supporting evidence. The example uses administrator-approved figures. The fund team resolves exceptions and approves investor communications, with valuation and sign-off responsibilities retained under its agreed arrangements. The page does not claim to perform trading, investment decisions, complete risk management, or independent assurance.

## What the examples prove—and what they do not

All website records, commentary, and outputs are fictional and prewritten. Interactions let visitors inspect the proposed document workflow, source records, figures, and review questions. They are not recordings of Cosimo generating these outputs, successful production proof runs, or customer results.

The examples explain the intended work. They do not substantiate a guaranteed processing time, hours saved, universal accuracy, autonomous delivery, audit readiness, or integration coverage. These workflows need configuration and testing with the fund team before making fund-specific capability commitments.

## How to start

Email info@medici.ai with a few sentences about the report or process your team prepares, where the information comes from, and which part takes the most time. Medici & Company will work through a first workflow to test with the team. Scope and commercial terms are agreed before starting. An evaluation uses one period of read-only source files under NDA, written feasibility confirmation, and a review of the output and sources. Model usage is charged at cost without markup; platform terms are agreed in conversation.

## Customer fit and responsibilities

Cosimo is for banks, funds, insurance teams, and financial service firms with recurring manual work. Fit depends on the specific process, records, and review requirements. Cosimo handles internal fund operations alongside outside providers; it is not currently the administrator of record. Accounting, valuation, professional sign-off, and investment decisions remain with the responsible people. Client data is restricted to that client’s work and is not used to train shared models.

## Tested product work

The October 2026 product deck documents daily production use by live clients, nine of ten RE processes tested figure by figure on synthetic demonstration funds, and 83 calculation scripts with 1,822 passing tests. A quarterly report run for five properties and eight investors matched figures to the cent against an 88-row source sheet and raised five exceptions. These are specific validation results, separate from the illustrative website walkthroughs, not universal accuracy or timing guarantees. Approval rules are configurable per process and user; the product can send authorized communications.
